narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='m1'/>Ten clicks of one hundred are fine, because they add to a thousand anyway.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>They do add to a thousand, but one click of one thousand does the same.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>That is nine clicks fewer, so the slip is struck out.
removed_beats.on_screen: the slip's bubble appears with ten clicks of one hundred; one click of one thousand sits beside them; the slip is struck through

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The fewest clicks never use a button ten or more times.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Each count is a digit, and the digits are the number.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>This is why place value notation is a short way of writing the fewest clicks.
removed_beats.on_screen: the words under ten clicks appear; the words counts are digits appear; the two forms are linked by an equals sign

old_misconception.wrong_move: A common slip allows ten clicks of one hundred. Ten clicks of one hundred are the same as one click of one thousand, so they are never needed.
